subject: MAP: Performance packaging and close plan (latency / TTFT / concurrency)
messages:
From: Claire Morris <claire@nimblestack.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP request: perf artifacts for Friday exec review

Hi Jordan / Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the trial access last week. The product team at NimbleStack wants a short performance appendix for our MAP so we can finish the exec readout on Friday. High level ask below: 

- One-slide summary of observed latency (p50 / p95) and throughput for our baseline prompts
- TTFT numbers (time-to-first-token) for chat flows
- Concurrency run summary (1 / 8 / 32 simulated users) and measured throughput
- CSV export of raw test runs (per-request timestamps, tokens, duration, error flags)
- Link to a live dashboard we can point to in the executive packet

Can you confirm you can deliver slides + CSV + dashboard link by close of business Friday 2026-06-11 PT? Also, we may need a 10-minute call on Friday morning to walk the execs through key takeaways.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Morris
Head of Product Operations, NimbleStack

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morris <claire@nimblestack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request: perf artifacts for Friday exec review

Hi Claire — can do. Quick plan and ownership below: 

Deliverables (by EOD Fri 2026-06-11 PT):
- 1-slide executive summary (latency / TTFT / concurrency highlights) — owner: Jordan
- Full slide deck with test methodology and readout notes — owner: Marissa
- CSV export of all runs + a cleaned summary CSV — owner: Karthik
- Live read-only dashboard link (time-series + per-run table) — owner: Jordan

Questions / constraints:
- Do you want the CSV to include full per-token timings or only per-request timings? We typically include per-request and sample per-token excerpts (adds size but helpful for TTFT verification).
- Do you have a target concurrency profile (beyond 1/8/32) or any expected peak tokens/sec to simulate?

We’ll run deterministic runs against the pinned model version you used in testing (redwood/atlas-v1.3) and include quantized/float variants only if you want them.

I’ll attach a brief scope doc so you can confirm. Assuming no unusual requests we’ll hit your deadline and can carve out Friday 09:00 PT for the exec walkthrough if that works.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Perf_Scope_v1.docx (docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Morris <claire@nimblestack.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request: perf artifacts for Friday exec review

Adding technical plan and CSV schema so Claire knows what to expect. Short version: we’ll run three controlled load points and capture per-request and sampled per-token timings for TTFT validation.

Benchmark plan (high level):
- Workload: 100 representative prompts provided by Claire (we’ll use the ones from the trial set)
- Model: redwood/atlas-v1.3 (fp16) pinned
- Load points:
  * Concurrency 1: cold-start runs x200 (measure TTFT distribution)
  * Concurrency 8: steady-state x500 (measure p50/p95 latency and throughput)
  * Concurrency 32: stress x200 (observe degradation/fallback behavior)
- Batch sizes: auto-batching enabled; we’ll report effective batch sizes and queueing delay
- Failure modes: rate-limited, OOM, unexpected errors — we’ll flag error counts in CSV

CSV schema (columns): run_id, timestamp_utc, concurrency, batch_size, request_tokens, response_tokens, time_to_first_token_ms, total_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, status, notes

I’m attaching short harness notes and a plan file. We’ll include the raw CSV and a cleaned summary CSV with aggregated p50/p95 and throughput rows. If you want sample raw per-token traces we can include those as a separate, compressed file.

- Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: perf_harness_notes.txt, benchmark-run-plan.yaml

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Claire Morris <claire@nimblestack.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request: perf artifacts for Friday exec review

Nice plan. For the executive packet please use the attached readout template (one slide headline + appendix slides). Jordan — please emphasize business impact: expected cost per 1M tokens at observed throughput and any recommendations (batching, KV cache policy) that materially change unit economics.

Claire — can you confirm final decision-maker(s) who will be in the Friday slot? I want to make sure we tailor the first-slide message appropriately (CFO vs Head of ML).

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Attachments: exec_readout_template.pptx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morris <claire@nimblestack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request: perf artifacts for Friday exec review — artifacts attached

Claire — attaching the deliverables per the MAP. Quick notes inline and a short executive summary below.

Attachments (zip of deliverables):
- Redwood_MAP_Perf_Slides_v1.pdf — 1-page executive headline + appendix
- benchmark_results_20260609.csv — cleaned run-level CSV (schema as shared)
- perf_harness_notes.txt — notes and commands to reproduce runs

Dashboard: https://redwood.app/dashboards/nimblestack-perf-2026 (read-only link)
HubSpot: https://crm.redwood.com/deals/NIM-2026-06-10-01

Executive summary (headline):
- Observed p50 latency (concurrency 8): 210 ms; p95: 560 ms; TTFT median (cold): 180 ms
- Throughput (concurrency 8): ~220 tokens/sec sustained; concurrency 32 shows graceful degradation to ~600 tokens/sec aggregate but p95 latency increases and queueing appears at backend edge
- Recommendation: enable prefix KV caching for session-heavy chat flows and prefer batch-size target of 8 where latency-sensitive — estimated cost improvement ~18% on token unit economics

Next steps: Confirm Friday 09:00 PT walkthrough (10 minutes) and I’ll join with Marissa and Karthik to do the live two-slide walk. If you want additional raw per-token CSVs we can attach as a follow-up.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Perf_Slides_v1.pdf (pdf), benchmark_results_20260609.csv (csv), perf_harness_notes.txt (txt)
